zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿إنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمّا عَلَيْها حافِظٌ﴾: its meaning is ”لَعَلَيْها حافِظٌ“ ("there is surely over it a guardian"), and ”ما“ is redundant (laghw). It was also read ”لَمّا عَلَيْها حافِطٌ“ with the doubled mīm (tashdīd), and then the meaning is the meaning of ”إلّا“ ("except"). ”لَمّا“ is used in the place of ”إلّا“ in two places: one of them is this, and the other is in the chapter of the oath; one says: ”سَألْتُكَ لَمّا فَعَلْتَ“ ("I ask you, by God, but that you do it"), meaning ”إلّا فَعَلْتَ“. [Translator's note: the source prints «حافِطٌ» with ṭāʾ in the second reading; this is evidently a misprint for «حافِظٌ».]

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خُلِقَ مِن ماءٍ دافِقٍ﴾ ("he was created from a gushing water"): its meaning is "from [what is] above" [Translator's note: so in the source, «مِن فَوْقَ»; it may be a corruption, e.g. of «مَدْفُوقٍ», "poured out"]. The doctrine of Sībawayh and his followers is that its meaning is attribution (nasab) to gushing; the meaning is ”مِن ماءِ ذِي انْدِفاقٍ“ ("from a water possessing gushing").

zajjaj:7-7.t:
And His saying: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِن بَيْنِ الصُّلْبِ والتَّرائِبِ﴾ ("it emerges from between the backbone and the tarāʾib"). ”اَلتَّرائِبُ“: it has come in the exegesis (tafsīr) that they are four ribs on the right side of the chest and four ribs on the left side of the chest; and it has come in the exegesis that the tarāʾib are the two hands, the two legs and the two eyes. The lexicographers all said: ”اَلتَّرائِبُ“ is the place of the necklace on the chest, and they recited for Imruʾ al-Qays:
مُهَفْهَفَةٌ بَيْضاءُ غَيْرُ مُفاضَةٍ ∗∗∗ تَرائِبُها مَصْقُولَةٌ كالسَّجَنْجَلِ
(Slender-waisted, fair, not flabby-bellied; her breastbones [tarāʾib] polished like a mirror.)

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ عَلى رَجْعِهِ لَقادِرٌ﴾ ("He is surely able to return it"): it has come in the exegesis: He is surely able to return the water to the urethra; and it has also come: to return it to the backbone; and it has also come: to return him, i.e. to resurrect the human being. This last is supported by His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تُبْلى السَّرائِرُ﴾ [al-Ṭāriq: 9] ("the Day when secrets are put to the test"), that is: He is able to resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection.

zajjaj:11-12.t:
And His saying: ﴿والسَّماءِ ذاتِ الرَّجْعِ﴾ ﴿والأرْضِ ذاتِ الصَّدْعِ﴾: ”ذاتِ الرَّجْعِ“ means "possessing rain", because it comes, returns and recurs. Abū ʿUbayda said: ”اَلرَّجْعُ“ is water, and he recited the verse of al-Munakhkhal al-Hudhalī:
أبْيَضُ كالرَّجْعِ رَسُوبٌ إذا ∗∗∗ ما ثاخَ في مُحْتَفَلٍ يَخْتَلِي
(White like water [al-rajʿ], deep-sinking; when it plunges into the thick of a body it cuts through.)
He said: he is describing the sword; he says: it is white like water.
﴿والأرْضِ ذاتِ الصَّدْعِ﴾: that is, it splits open with vegetation.

zajjaj:13-13.t: ﴿إنَّهُ لَقَوْلٌ فَصْلٌ﴾ ("it is surely a decisive word"): this is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam). By it the Qur'an is meant; it decides between truth and falsehood.

zajjaj:14-14.t: ﴿وَما هو بِالهَزْلِ﴾: it is not frivolous play (laʿib).

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿إنَّهم يَكِيدُونَ كَيْدًا﴾ ("they are plotting a plot"): He means by it the unbelievers: that they practise deceit against the Prophet, peace be upon him, and display the opposite of what they are.

zajjaj:16-16.t: ﴿وَأكِيدُ كَيْدًا﴾ ("and I am plotting a plot"): Allah's plotting against them is His drawing them on step by step (istidrāj) from where they do not know.

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أمْهِلْهم رُوَيْدًا﴾: that is, give them respite for a little while.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ṭāriq
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿والسَّماءِ والطّارِقِ﴾: the answer to the oath is: ﴿إنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمّا عَلَيْها حافِظٌ﴾ [al-Ṭāriq: 4]. «اَلطّارِقُ» is the star, and by «اَلنَّجْمُ» (the star) the stars are meant. The star is called «طارِقٌ» (night-comer) only because its rising is at night, and everything that comes by night is a ṭāriq, because the night is a time in which one is still. From this it is said «أطْرَقَ فُلانٌ» when someone refrains from speaking and is still.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And ﴿الثّاقِبُ﴾ is the shining one. One says «ثَقَبَ، يَثْقُبُ، ثُقُوبًا» when it shines, and one says to the one kindling a fire: «أثْقِبْ نارَكَ», that is: make it blaze.
